gloss: vanity; showing off; keeping up appearances

definitions.gloss: vanity; showing off; putting on airs
definitions.explanation: The act of trying to appear better, wealthier, or more capable than one actually is.
A stylized, dramatic pose struck by kabuki actors at climactic moments.

examples.japanese: {見栄|みえ}を{張|は}って{高|たか}い{車|くるま}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought an expensive car to show off.

examples.japanese: {見栄|みえ}っ{張|ぱ}りな{性格|せいかく}を{直|なお}したい。
examples.english: I want to fix my habit of showing off.

examples.japanese: {歌舞伎|かぶき}{役者|やくしゃ}が{見栄|みえ}を{切|き}った。
examples.english: The kabuki actor struck a dramatic pose.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{見栄|みえ}を{張|は}る (to show off, to put on airs)
・{見栄|みえ}っ{張|ぱ}り (noun/na-adj: show-off, vain person)
・{見栄|みえ}を{切|き}る (to strike a dramatic pose - kabuki term)

KABUKI ORIGIN:
The theatrical term ({見栄|みえ}を{切|き}る) refers to the stylized pose where actors cross their eyes, turn their head sharply, and freeze at a dramatic moment. This pose emphasizes emotion and is unique to kabuki.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{虚栄心|きょえいしん} (vanity, conceit) - more abstract, internal feeling
・{見栄|みえ} focuses on the outward display of vanity

NUANCE:
{見栄|みえ}を{張|は}る often implies spending beyond one's means or pretending to be more successful than one is.
